body:
`InterestRate::impliedRate` returned a constant 0 whenever the compound factor was 1. That's correct for `double`, but with AD types it drops the dependence on the inputs, so sensitivities through a zero rate come out as zero. The shortcut is now limited to t = 0. For t > 0 the regular formulas already give exactly 0.

Tested: the test suite passes, and `double` results are unchanged. With AD, an American option's dividend rho at zero dividend yield now matches finite differences.
title: Keep the derivative of an implied rate when the compound factor is 1
